title: Object-fit and object-position
learningObjectives: Explain object-fit and object-position and use the relevant CSS properties appropriately.

understand.concept: object-fit controls how replaced content such as an image or video is resized within its specified box. Common values include cover, contain, fill, none, and scale-down. object-position controls which part of the content is aligned within the box.
understand.whyItMatters: cover may crop parts of an image; contain may leave empty space. For meaningful images, preserve appropriate alternative text and choose cropping that does not remove essential visual information.
understand.analogy: object-fit is like choosing how a photograph sits inside a fixed frame: fill the frame by cropping, or show the whole image with unused space.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy helps visualise the effect; CSS rendering and stacking follow browser layout and painting rules.

explain.narrative: Replace the illustrative URL with an image you are allowed to use. The fixed image box crops using cover and shifts the focal position slightly upward.

practise.guidedTask: Compare cover and contain on the same image. Change object-position to keep the subject visible.
practise.independentTask: Build a small component that uses this visual treatment without reducing readability or keyboard usability.
hints: Inspect the rendered result against different backgrounds.
Change one property at a time.
Keep focus indicators visible and content readable.

questions.prompt: Which object-fit value fills the box while preserving aspect ratio and potentially cropping?
questions.explanation: cover fills the content box while preserving aspect ratio, potentially cropping.

questions.prompt: What should you verify when adding decorative visual effects?
options: Only whether the effect looks fashionable
Whether the effect hides focus outlines
questions.explanation: Visual effects should not make content or interactive states harder to perceive.
